steps.say: Cancer of the gallbladder grows where stones have irritated for years. Big stones, a chalky calcified wall and certain regions of the world carry far higher risk, with women affected most.
steps.tx: Gallstones over **3 cm** (three centimetres), **porcelain calcification** (chalky wall) and polyps over **10 mm** (ten millimetres) raise gallbladder cancer risk, endemic in North India with striking female predominance and late presentation at advanced stages with poor outlook unless caught early by chance.

vis.alt: Tumour at the gallbladder neck with stones, calcified wall and nearby draining glands.
vis.caption: Gallbladder cancer: tumour with gallstones, porcelain wall change and regional nodes. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: A cancer found by accident after a routine removal behaves very differently by depth. Disease still in the lining needs nothing more, while muscle invasion demands a second, bigger operation.
steps.tx: Incidental **T1a** (mucosa-only) **incidental gallbladder cancer** (surprise early tumour) after simple cholecystectomy needs no further surgery with 5-year survival near **100 percent** (near total cure), while **T1b** (muscle invasion) needs extended resection with full nodal clearance for cure in fit surgical candidates.

steps.say: The second operation takes a rim of liver around the gallbladder bed plus all the nearby glands. A two-centimetre cuff of liver and a full packet of nodes turn an accident into a cure.
steps.tx: **Extended cholecystectomy** (liver-rim gallbladder removal) takes segments **IVb and V** (four B and five) with **2 cm** (two centimetre) margins plus **portal nodal clearance** (gland packet removal) of at least **6 nodes** (six glands) for T1b and T2 disease, converting surprise into cure.

steps.say: Tumours bursting through the wall or gripping big vessels start with drugs, not the knife. Only cancers that shrink and show no distant spread on repeat scans earn an operation.
steps.tx: **T3** (through-wall) disease breaching serosa and **T4** (vessel-gripping) disease with vascular invasion get **neoadjuvant** (pre-surgery) gemcitabine-cisplatin first, with surgery only for responders without distant spread on careful restaging scans after chemotherapy courses finish fully and a clear response is confirmed on imaging.

steps.say: Yellow eyes at first visit usually mean the growth has reached the main pipes where no knife can follow. A metal tube placed through the blockage restores flow and buys months.
steps.tx: Jaundice at presentation usually marks unresectable hilar invasion, and palliation uses endoscopic **metal stenting** (spring tube drainage) with **8 to 12 month** (eight to twelve month) patency plus pain and sepsis control by the palliative team throughout the remaining illness.

steps.say: Keyhole surgery for what looked like stones can scatter hidden cancer to the small cuts. Those scars must be cut out widely together with the main specimen when the diagnosis lands.
steps.tx: **Port-site recurrence** (wound seeding after laparoscopy) for unsuspected cancer mandates **port excision** (scar removal) of all port sites together with the definitive resection specimen at radical reoperation without delay once the surprise diagnosis is fully confirmed by pathology review urgently.

steps.say: Even after a clean removal, tablets for half a year improve the odds. The BILCAP study proved this, and close scanning catches the few recurrences early enough to act.
steps.tx: Adjuvant **capecitabine** (post-surgery tablets) for **6 months** (six months) after R0 resection improves survival per **BILCAP** (adjuvant trial), with surveillance using **3-monthly** (quarterly) imaging to catch the early recurrence peak when action still helps and cure remains possible after salvage.

steps.say: Not every thick-walled gallbladder is cancer. A fierce but benign inflammation swells the wall and sticks to everything nearby, and only a microscope sample during surgery tells the two apart.
steps.tx: **Xanthogranulomatous cholecystitis** (granuloma wall disease) mimics cancer with wall thickening and infiltration, distinguished by intact mucosa on imaging and **frozen section** (instant microscopy) at surgery before any radical steps are taken in the operating theatre that day by the surgeon.
